hints.title: Consider Passenger Assignment
hints.text: Each passenger can only board the earliest bus that arrives at or after their arrival time.

hints.title: Map Each Passenger to Bus Arrival
hints.text: Join passengers with buses on passenger arrival time less than or equal to bus arrival time and take the minimum bus arrival time per passenger.

hints.title: Aggregate Passengers per Bus
hints.text: Left join the original buses table with the passenger bus assignments on arrival time, then count the matched passengers grouping by bus identifier.

hints.title: Complete SQL Query
hints.text:
```sql
WITH PassengerBus AS (
    SELECT p.passenger_id, MIN(b.arrival_time) AS bus_arrival_time
    FROM Passengers p
    JOIN Buses b ON p.arrival_time <= b.arrival_time
    GROUP BY p.passenger_id
)
SELECT b.bus_id, COUNT(pb.passenger_id) AS passengers_cnt
FROM Buses b
LEFT JOIN PassengerBus pb ON b.arrival_time = pb.bus_arrival_time
GROUP BY b.bus_id
ORDER BY b.bus_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) query execution and joins
variables: N: input size or row count
complexity.whyNaiveFails: A simple Cartesian join without isolating the earliest matching bus for each passenger results in passengers being counted for every subsequent bus.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping passengers by identifier to find the minimum arrival bus takes O(P * B) worst-case or O((P + B) log B) with indexing, requiring O(P) auxiliary CTE storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Demonstrate mastery of grouping over inequalities and joining back to preserve buses with zero boarding passengers.
